p.src: Overview: Entanglement can be created and undone by reversible dynamics, yet measurements become effectively irreversible when part of the entangled system escapes our control. That distinction leads to a precise locality test: Bob may apply any unitary operation in his neighborhood, but Alice’s reduced density matrix, and therefore every statistic available to her alone, remains unchanged. A classical-simulation thought experiment then isolates what is genuinely nonclassical. One spin is easy to imitate, and a central computer can imitate an entangled pair, but separated local machines cannot reproduce all entangled correlations without illicit communication or a Bell-local hidden-variable model that ultimately fails. The lecture then leaves spins for a particle on a line. Discrete sums become integrals, Kronecker deltas become Dirac deltas, and wave functions become vectors in an infinite-dimensional space. Multiplication by $x$ gives position; differentiation is anti-Hermitian; multiplying it by $-i$ produces the Hermitian momentum operator. The final calculation, $[x,p]=i\hbar$, reconnects quantum commutators with classical Poisson brackets and points toward wave packets, Fourier transforms, and Schrödinger evolution.

p.src: Entanglement Is Not Irreversibility

u.src: Entanglement Is Not Irreversibility
en: Entanglement Is Not Irreversibility
ja: エンタングルメントは不可逆性ではない
zh: 纠缠并非不可逆性

p.src: Begin with a distinction that is easy to lose in discussions of measurement. Suppose two spins arrive in a product state, interact, separate, and leave in an entangled state. Must the entanglement remain forever? No. The interaction was unitary, so another suitable interaction can undo it. One may reflect the spins, bring them together again, and arrange an inverse evolution that returns the pair to a product state. There is no law according to which entanglement itself only increases.

ja: 測定の議論で見失いやすい区別から始めよう。2つのスピンが積状態で到着し、相互作用し、離れてエンタングル状態になったとしよう。エンタングルメントは永遠に残らなければならないのだろうか。否。その相互作用はユニタリであったから、別の適切な相互作用がそれを解消できる。スピンを反射し、再び近づけ、対を積状態に戻す逆の時間発展を用意すればよい。エンタングルメント自体が増大するだけであるという法則は存在しない。
zh: 先从一个在测量讨论中容易丢失的区别开始。假设两个自旋以乘积态到达，发生相互作用，分离，并以纠缠态离开。纠缠必须永远保持吗？不。相互作用是幺正的，所以另一个合适的相互作用可以将其消除。人们可以反射这两个自旋，使它们再次靠近，并安排一个逆演化，使这一对回到乘积态。并不存在一条定律说纠缠本身只会增加。

p.src: The situation changes operationally when one member of the pair is discarded. If an electron flies away into an uncontrolled environment, then the partner that remains nearby is still entangled with something, but the missing degrees of freedom are no longer available for the inverse operation. In principle the distant electron might be reflected back; in practice it is gone. This is the sense in which a measurement is irreversible for us: the correlations have spread into degrees of freedom that we do not control.

ja: 対の一方が捨てられると、状況は操作的に変わる。電子が制御されない環境へ飛び去ってしまえば、近くに残った相方は依然として何かとエンタングルしているが、失われた自由度はもはや逆操作に利用できない。原理的には遠方の電子を反射して戻せるかもしれないが、実際にはそれは失われている。これが、測定が我々にとって不可逆であるという意味である。すなわち、相関が我々の制御しない自由度へ広がってしまったのである。
zh: 当这一对中的一个成员被丢弃时，情况在操作层面就改变了。如果一个电子飞入不受控制的环境，那么留在附近的伙伴仍然与某物纠缠，但缺失的自由度不再可用于逆操作。原则上，远处的电子也许可以被反射回来；实际上，它已经消失了。这就是测量对我们而言不可逆的意义：关联已经扩散到我们无法控制的自由度中。

ja: 受講者からの質問: 2つの系がエンタングルしたなら、後にエンタングルを解くことはできますか。
zh: 听众提问: 如果两个系统变得纠缠，它们之后能变得不纠缠吗？

p.src: Response: Yes. Unitary evolution is reversible. A second interaction can implement the inverse of the first and restore a product state. Irreversibility enters when relevant degrees of freedom are thrown away or absorbed into an uncontrolled environment, not from entanglement alone.

p.src: The State Available to Alice

u.src: The State Available to Alice
en: The State Available to Alice
ja: アリスが利用できる状態
zh: Alice可用的状态

p.src:
Let a composite system be divided into Alice’s degrees of freedom $a$ and Bob’s degrees of freedom $b$, with pure-state coefficients $\Psi(a,b)=\braket{a,b}{\Psi}.$ Alice does not have access to Bob’s laboratory. Her complete local description is therefore not generally a wave function. It is the reduced density matrix $\rho_A(a',a)
=
\sum_b \Psi^*(a',b)\Psi(a,b).$ The sum removes Bob’s label. What remains has one bra index and one ket index for Alice, and it contains every probability distribution that Alice can obtain by experiments performed entirely in her neighborhood.

\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\rho_{B\mid A=\text{click}}$ is the distinction between no signaling and useful correlations.

p.src: The Einstein–Podolsky–Rosen discomfort nevertheless survives. A singlet can give us maximal knowledge of the whole while neither constituent has a pure local state. To expose the peculiarity more sharply, turn quantum mechanics into a programming problem.

The lecture leaves the metaphysics open while retaining the experimental premise.

u.src: Position by multiplication
en: Position by multiplication
ja: 掛け算による位置

p.src:
The simplest operator multiplies a wave function by the coordinate: $(x\psi)(x)=x\psi(x).$ It is linear, and $\begin{aligned}\braket{\phi}{x\psi}
&=
\int dx\,\phi^*(x)x\psi(x), \notag\\
\braket{x\phi}{\psi}
&=
\int dx\,[x\phi(x)]^*\psi(x) \notag\\
&=
\int dx\,\phi^*(x)x\psi(x),\end{aligned}$ because $x$ is real. Multiplication by $x$ is therefore Hermitian and represents the position observable.

en: Differentiation is anti-Hermitian

p.src:
Try the derivative $D=\frac{d}{dx}.$ It is linear, but integration by parts gives $\begin{aligned}\braket{\phi}{D\psi}
&=
\int dx\,\phi^*(x)\frac{d\psi}{dx} \notag\\
&=
\left[\phi^*(x)\psi(x)\right]_{-\infty}^{\infty}
-
\int dx\,\frac{d\phi^*}{dx}\psi(x) \notag\\
&=
-\braket{D\phi}{\psi},
\end{aligned}$ where the boundary term vanishes. Thus $D^\dagger=-D.$ The derivative is anti-Hermitian rather than Hermitian.
